chief_complaint: recurrent, painful, draining boils, sinus tracts, and rope-like scarring in bilateral axillae and groin
hpi_details: 32F smoker presenting with Hurley Stage II Hidradenitis Suppurativa with tender abscesses and interconnecting fistulas requiring prolonged oral Clindamycin plus Rifampin, intralesional triamcinolone, and consideration of Adalimumab.
ideas: She thinks the painful draining lumps are chronic ingrown hairs and infected sweat glands caused by shaving and deodorant buildup.
concerns: She is terrified that the foul-smelling fluid will leak through her work clothes during meetings and that her partner will find her body repulsive.
expectations: She hopes to have the most painful boils lanced and drained today and get a prescription for a strong painkiller and antibiotic wash.

core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Hidradenitis Suppurativa is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.

Standard management of Hidradenitis Suppurativa is staged by Hurley severity, combining smoking cessation, antibiotics (e.g., clindamycin plus rifampin) for moderate disease, and biologic therapy such as adalimumab for refractory cases.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: recurrent, painful, draining boils, sinus tracts, and rope-like scarring in bilateral axillae and groin

Key HPI features: 32F smoker presenting with Hurley Stage II Hidradenitis Suppurativa with tender abscesses and interconnecting fistulas requiring prolonged oral Clindamycin plus Rifampin, intralesional triamcinolone, and consideration of Adalimumab.
Objective/Exam findings: Tender inflammatory nodules, abscesses, and interconnecting draining sinus tracts with rope-like fibrotic scarring in the bilateral axillae and groin.
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Hidradenitis Suppurativa.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Recurrent furunculosis (simple boils) without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Fever with spreading redness — suggests a more severe abscess or cellulitis needing urgent drainage.
management_principles: Stage disease severity using the Hurley classification to guide treatment intensity.
Strongly counsel smoking cessation and weight management as key modifiable risk factors.
Use oral clindamycin plus rifampin for moderate (Hurley II) disease, with intralesional triamcinolone for acute flares.
Escalate to biologic therapy (e.g., adalimumab) or refer to dermatology/surgery for refractory or Hurley III disease.
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

teaching.one_liner: A chronic inflammatory disease of hair follicles in skin fold areas (armpits, groin), causing recurrent painful boils, draining sinus tracts, and rope-like scarring — strongly linked to smoking and obesity.
red_flags: Fever with spreading redness — suggests a more severe abscess or cellulitis needing urgent drainage

must_ask.say: Where do the boils occur, and how often do they come back?
Do they drain pus, and have they left scarring or tunnels under the skin?
How painful are these, and how do they affect your daily life?
Does this condition run in your family?

history.answer: I keep getting these painful, swollen lumps under both my armpits and in my groin that burst open, drain foul-smelling pus, and leave thick ropy scars.
These boils first started about two years ago as tender bumps under my arms, but over the last six months they have gotten much worse and spread down into my groin creases.
They only show up in my skin folds, specifically under both armpits and along both sides of my groin. I do not have them on my face, chest, hands, or feet.
They swell into deep, painful boils that eventually rupture and leak yellow, blood-tinged pus, and as they heal they form thick, rope-like cords under my skin.
They throb and hurt constantly, especially when my skin rubs together or when I move my arms. They do not really itch, but they feel tender and tight.
No, these are not hives that fade in a few hours. Each painful lump builds up over days, stays inflamed for weeks, and leaves permanent tunnels and scars.
I have had multiple flare-ups over the past two years. An urgent care doctor lanced one boil last year and gave me a short round of antibiotics, but the lumps came right back.
It is exhausting and embarrassing because the drainage stains my clothes and the pain makes it hard to lift my arms at work or exercise.
No, I have not had any fever, chills, or whole-body aches.
The skin around the boils is red and inflamed, but I haven't noticed any rapidly spreading redness or red streaks moving up my skin.
No stomach pain, chronic diarrhea, or bleeding from my bowels at all.
No, I don't have any sores in my mouth, eye irritation, or ulcers on my genital mucosa.
No, my skin is not peeling off anywhere, and I don't have any dark purple spots or bruises.
No, I have never had swelling of my lips, tongue, or face, and my breathing has been completely normal.
I haven't started using any new laundry detergents, deodorants, cosmetics, or perfumes, and I don't wear nickel jewelry in those areas.
No, I haven't been bitten by insects, and I haven't gone hiking, traveling, or using public saunas or swimming pools.
I have never had eczema, atopic dermatitis, asthma, or allergic rhinitis.
No joint stiffness or swelling, and my fingernails look completely normal without pitting.
I tried putting over-the-counter hydrocortisone cream and an antibacterial ointment on them, but neither helped at all.
No, I haven't started any new prescription drugs or supplements recently.
I thought I just kept getting terrible infected ingrown hairs and blocked sweat glands from shaving my underarms and bikini line.
I'm terrified that the drainage will seep through my work clothes and smell during a meeting, and that my partner is going to be completely disgusted by my body.
I was hoping you could lance and drain the biggest boil today so I can walk comfortably, and give me a strong antibiotic wash to stop the drainage.
I have high blood pressure and slightly high cholesterol. No history of diabetes or autoimmune conditions.
No major surgeries or hospital admissions, other than having one boil drained at urgent care last year.
I take Lisinopril 10 milligrams once a day for my blood pressure. I am not taking anything else right now.
I do not have any known allergies to medications.
I smoke about half a pack of cigarettes a day and have been smoking for the past ten years.
I drink socially, maybe one or two glasses of wine a month.
I work in an office as an administrative assistant and live in an apartment with my husband.
My mother used to get painful cysts under her arms that she called boils, though she was never formally diagnosed.
I have been with my husband for six years. I have never had genital herpes, syphilis, or any sexually transmitted infection.
My last period began two weeks ago, my monthly cycles are regular, we use condoms for contraception, and there is no chance I am pregnant.

exam.finding: Blood pressure 128/82 mmHg, heart rate 76 beats/min, respiratory rate 14 breaths/min, body temperature 36.8°C, oxygen saturation 99% on room air.
Alert woman, moving her arms guardedly due to axillary discomfort, in no acute distress.

Bilateral axillary vaults demonstrate tender erythematous nodules, fluctuant abscesses, interconnecting sinus tracts discharging purulent exudate, and thick rope-like fibrotic bands; breast tissue is normal without masses.
Tender inflammatory nodules and draining sinus tracts along both groin creases with bridged cord-like scars; no inguinal hernia detected.
No generalized rash; skin outside the axillary and inguinal folds is intact, clear, and without unblanchable purpura or epidermolysis.
External genitalia show no mucosal ulcers, chancres, or blisters; lesions are restricted to the skin folds.
Conjunctivae are non-injected and pink without discharge; sclerae are anicteric.
Oral mucosa is moist and pink without ulcers, erosions, or plaques; posterior pharynx is clear.
No cervical or supraclavicular lymphadenopathy noted.
Abdomen is soft, non-tender throughout, with active bowel sounds and no palpable masses or hepatosplenomegaly.
No joint swelling, warmth, or deformity; peripheral fingernails and toenails are normal without pitting or dystrophy.
